thread:
support-bot: Incoming escalation from Support — AcmeFin reporting sudden p99 spike after midnight deploy. p50 ~80ms, p95 ~300ms, p99 ~1.8s for text-generation short prompts. Started ~00:10 UTC; ~40% of requests affected. Looks like continuous batching change landed last night.

maya: I'm on it. Who merged the runtime change around 00:00? @sam @liam

sam: That was me. Merged config tweak to continuous-batcher defaults to improve throughput for small requests: increased max_batch_size 64->128 and lowered min_wait_ms 20->8. Can roll back if needed.

liam: tagging @anika for metrics. Maya, can you paste an example req id or trace? Support mentioned req_id af-req-92e7.

anika: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/batcher-latency?orgId=1&var-environment=prod

anika: Quick snapshot: overall p50 75ms (same); p95 210->320ms at 00:11; p99 450->1.8s at 00:12. Batch size dist: median 12->48, tail up to ~110.

maya: sounds like bigger batches mixing requests -> head-of-line blocking. Need repro + mitigation. @sam can you revert canary to previous batching config ASAP?

sam: diff that landed:
```
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_size: 128    # was 64
  min_wait_ms: 8         # was 20
  batching_strategy: adaptive
```
Proposed immediate canary revert:
```
continuous_batching:
  max_batch_size: 64
  min_wait_ms: 20
```
I'll patch canary in ~5m.

maya: also add quick per-customer max_batch_size override for AcmeFin -> 32 so we don't have to revert globally.

jorge: logs for req_id grep: 
```
[00:11:52] batcher: dispatch batch_id=374 size=110 wait_ms=9 latency_ms_avg=210 tail=1800 customer=acme-fin
[00:11:52] model: start token gen for batch=374
[00:12:00] model: token 1 took 600ms for seq_len 32
[00:12:01] batcher: complete batch_id=374 total_ms=1820
```

devon: one slow request in the batch likely held up the whole batch.

maya: action plan: 1) Sam patch canary to old defaults (max_batch_size=64, min_wait_ms=20) and watch p99. 2) If canary good -> roll prod; else rollback. 3) Per-customer cap for AcmeFin to 32. 4) Short-term rule to avoid mixing high-latency sessions in same batch (route by session_quality tag).

sam: applied canary patch at 00:25 UTC to 2/8 canary pods. Command run:
```
kubectl -n runtime patch deploy batcher-canary --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"{\\"max_batch_size\\":64,\\"min_wait_ms\\":20}"}]'
```
Monitoring now. Grafana shows canary p99 drop 1.8s -> 420ms within 2m for canary slice.

anika: prometheus query used:
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(batcher_request_duration_seconds_bucket{env="prod",slice="canary"}[2m])) by (le))
```
Query result ~0.42s at 00:28.

support-bot: Support updated AcmeFin at 00:30: "Investigating root cause and applied temporary constraints; will follow up in 30m." Customer reports partial improvement.

maya: can we roll changes to full prod? Canary looks good. Any objections to a gradual rollout?

liam: proceed with gradual rolling restart + monitor. Also add AB tests to compare quantized vs non-quantized latency per batch to rule out model-side long token steps.

sam: started rollout at 00:40 UTC (`kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/batcher CONT_BATCH_CFG='{"max_batch_size":64,"min_wait_ms":20}' --record`). Rolling update completed 00:55 UTC.

anika: prod p99 timeline: spike at 00:11 -> partial recovery 00:28 -> decline 00:50 -> baseline ~480ms by 00:58.

devon: Support verification — AcmeFin sees p99 ~500ms now, much improved.

support-bot: AcmeFin notified 01:12: "Big improvement, thanks. A few requests still slow but much better."

maya: root cause draft: lowering min_wait_ms + raising max_batch_size caused heterogeneous arrival grouping into very large batches. Any single slow request (heavy token step) caused head-of-line latency -> p99 regression. We also lack customer isolation by inferred token-cost so batches mix heavy/light sessions.

maya: immediate mitigations taken: reverted global defaults after canary test; applied per-customer batch cap for AcmeFin; created follow-up for per-customer batching policy and heuristic to limit batch mixing.

anika: opening PR for alert rule to detect sudden batch size distribution shift + p99 spike.

liam: postmortem follow-ups: automated safe-rollback on config changes (trigger on p99 threshold), synthetic mixed-latency test, runtime knob for per-customer max_batch_size and labels for token-cost routing, improve logging to include per-batch session ids.

maya: repro steps for engineers: 1) set continuous batching min_wait_ms <=10 and max_batch_size >=100. 2) run mixed clients: 80% quick small requests, 20% expensive long-step requests. 3) observe batch size shift and p99 jump in 5-15m.

sam: local repro harness snippet:
```
# run 1000 requests, 200 heavy
python tools/repro/mixed_batch_test.py --clients 100 --heavy_ratio 0.2 --min_wait_ms 8 --max_batch_size 128
```

maya: closing loop with Support; send summary + ETA for fixes (per-customer policy + automated rollback) in PM. @support-bot please notify AcmeFin and mark escalation resolved if no follow-up.

support-bot: AcmeFin notified at 01:40 UTC; will re-open if they see anything. Escalation marked RESOLVED; monitoring for 24h.

maya: assigning action items: anika alert+dashboard PR owner; sam add canary automated rollback owner; liam repro harness + tests owner; devon instrument per-batch session ids owner.

maya: thanks all — will include timeline and config diff in incident postmortem.
